subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations / follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations / next steps

Hi Samir / team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on the regulatory constraints. Quick recap + a couple of clarifying questions so we can route the right folks and get the technical deep-dive scheduled.

Call recap (high level):
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation for customer inputs and outputs used by ML inference.
- Controls of interest: VPC-only access, private connectivity (PrivateLink / VPC peering), customer-managed KMS / HSM, audit logs and retention, and proof of model-weight residency/isolation.
- Expected scale: initial PoC ~50 qps peak, production target ~500 qps with 99th pct latency SLO ~200ms for text generation workloads.
- Timeline: PoC in next 6-8 weeks, procurement/regulatory sign-off shortly after.

Clarifying questions so we route correctly:
1) Do you require that model weights themselves never leave customer infrastructure (i.e., on-prem or customer-managed private deployment), or is single-tenant Dedicated capacity (Redwood-hosted GPUs dedicated to your tenant) acceptable if the control plane remains hosted?
2) Any strict egress prohibition (no third-party network calls permitted from the inference instances)?
3) Is US region-only residency required (we noted you mentioned us-east-1 on the call)?

What I can share right away:
- Short product comparison (Dedicated vs Private VPC vs On-prem) attached.
- SOC 2 summary (redacted) attached.

Next steps I suggest:
- Technical deep-dive with Mateo (infrastructure lead) to validate network/topology requirements and confirm whether Dedicated can meet your isolation constraints OR if Private (VPC/On-prem) is necessary.
- Legal/procurement intro for MSA/NDA and timing — I'll loop in our contracts team once you confirm interest.

Can you confirm answers to the three clarifying questions above? If agreeable, Mateo and I are available for a 60-minute deep-dive next week (Tue/Wed afternoon PT).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finsecure.com>

Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations / follow-up

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers:

1) Ideally model weights should be isolated from any shared Redwood infrastructure. Our compliance team is pushing for the option where model artifacts are under our control (either deployed to a Private VPC where control plane and weights are isolated, or an on-prem deployment). If Dedicated means dedicated GPUs but Redwood still manages model artifacts in your control plane, that will likely not be sufficient for our regulators.
2) Yes — minimal allowed egress. PoC can have limited outbound for monitoring but production should not allow arbitrary third-party network calls from inference instances.
3) Yes — US-only, specifically us-east-1 for data residency.

I'll attach our security questionnaire (finsecure_security_questionnaire.docx) — it's a bit long but highlights the exact controls we need.

We should definitely do the deep-dive with your infra engineer. Tu/Wed afternoons next week work.

Samir Patel

Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations / follow-up

Hi Samir — great, thanks for the clear answers and for sending the questionnaire.

Short response/high-level on options:
- Dedicated (Reserved Capacity): single-tenant GPU pools where your inference workload runs isolated on dedicated hardware. Control plane (orchestration, model artifact storage, and some management APIs) remains hosted by Redwood unless combined with Private control plane options. Dedicated alone typically does not meet the requirement for customer-managed model artifact residency.
- Private VPC (hosted private control plane): we can offer a Private deployment where the control plane is provisioned into your VPC (or connected via private networking) and model artifacts remain in resources under your account, with customer-managed KMS. This configuration meets the majority of strict data isolation requirements while still allowing Redwood-managed operational tooling via private connectivity.
- On-prem / Air-gapped: for the strictest regulatory needs, we offer an on-prem package where both control plane and runtime are deployed in your environment; this gives you full control over model weights and eliminates outbound egress except what you allow.

Given your answers, Private VPC or On-prem are the two paths that align with regulators' expectations. From here I suggest:
1) Technical deep-dive (60 min) — Mateo to walk network topology, VPC endpoints, routing, and KMS integrations.
2) Security review — Rachel can coordinate to map your questionnaire items to our artifacts (SOC2, penetration test summaries, architecture diagrams).
3) Procurement/legal — I'll start an internal intake so we can have an NDA/MSA draft ready after the deep-dive.

Proposed times for the deep-dive (all PT): Tue Jun 1 2:00-3:00pm or Wed Jun 2 3:00-4:00pm. Which works better?
